questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good replacement for either one.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your riding ability?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they usually do not affect your riding ability.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding ability. Always check the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden movements.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Never count on it.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
It is best used by itself.
It should sometimes assist the rear brake.
It should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to straighten out after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when you accelerate?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates uncontrollably.
It makes acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. When you accelerate, it lags behind because of its weight and inertia.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do with the handgrip?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip in the opposite direction of your turn.
Do not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn causes the proper lean.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only about five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals and brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be prepared to avoid an unexpected hazard.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Brake on the tire that is not flat.
Brake on the tire that is flat.
Brake on both tires.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly brake on the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one it is).

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is correct?

options.text: You must complete the pass without going over the speed limit.
You can finish passing in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can go over the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without going over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must happen within the speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe when using only the front brake.
Safe when using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you need the right technique and must be very careful.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you learn how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: You should keep more space between you and other vehicles when:

options.text: Roads are slippery.
It is sunny outside.
It is colder than usual.
You are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: Keep more space between you and other vehicles when conditions make stopping harder, such as when the road is icy or wet. A two-second following distance is normal under good conditions.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than during the day under the same conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than during the day under the same conditions.
On the shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day under similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so going slower helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay out of the left part of your lane.
Always stay out of the right part of your lane.
Always stay out of the center of your lane.
Use whatever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: The previous owner.
The owner's manual.
A library book about motorcycles.
A motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before operating your motorcycle for the first time.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: If you are 21 or older and have a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher, you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn can:

options.text: Not be used.
Usually not be heard by other drivers.
Alert someone quickly.
Never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert someone quickly.
questions.explanation: A horn helps get someone's attention fast. But a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of a lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean with you.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They should hold onto passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and let it correct itself.
Brake hard quickly.
Close the throttle slowly to stop speeding.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle slowly to stop speeding.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tight, slow down by closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Once off the road, find what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Instead of turn signals, riders use hand signals. When a rider's left arm is straight out to the left, they are turning left or moving left into another lane.
